{{Short description|American physicist}}
'''Richard Peter Majeski''' (born March 14, 1952) is an American [[physicist]] from the [[Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite book |title=Scientific and Technical Aerospace Reports |date=1979 |publisher=Scientific and Technical Information Branch, National Aeronautics and Space Administration |page=3287 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=lt7-Z4ffUF4C&dq=%22Richard+Peter+Majeski%22+physics&pg=PA3287 |accessdate=30 December 2019 |language=en}}</ref> He earned his bachelor's (1973) and master's (1974) degrees from the [[University of Scranton]] and his PhD in physics from [[Dartmouth College]] (1979).<ref>{{cite news |title=R. P. Majeski has doctorate |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/535583971/?terms=Richard%2BP.%2BMajeski |accessdate=December 30, 2019 |work=[[The Scranton Times-Tribune]] |date=June 21, 1979 |location=Scranton, Pennsylvania |page=9 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

He was awarded the status of Fellow in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> after they were nominated by their Division of [[Plasma (physics)|Plasma Physics]]  in 2007,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2007&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2007|website=www.aps.org|language=en|access-date=2017-04-20}}</ref> for ''fundamental studies of [[Radio frequency|radio-frequency]] heating and plasma-wall interactions, including the first observation of [[Alfvén wave|Alfvén]] wave heating in a [[tokamak]], the first demonstration of [[Mode conversion|mode-conversion]] current drive, and pioneering work in the use of liquid [[lithium]] as a [[Plasma-facing material|plasma-facing]] component.''
